content:
ops-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher pool 'cb-uswest-2' reporting sustained latency > 10s and 5xx spike, auto-paging @eng-oncall @eng-sre
leah (eng-oncall): I'm on it, pulling up dashboards now. seeing steady batch queue growth + memory climb on 3 nodes
sam (eng-runtime): flags in logs show kvcache size ramping; CPU fine but GPU memory creeping then OOM on one pod
leah (eng-oncall): logs snippet: ```2026-03-15T09:01:23Z ERROR runtime: CUDA OOM allocating 1024 MiB at /app/infer.cu:432
2026-03-15T09:01:24Z WARN batcher: accumulator length 1.9M tokens, kv_cache_bytes=12.4GiB```
raj (eng-sre): node flare on ip-10-0-12-45 — kernel OOM killer killed containerd? getting kube events now
carlos (prod-support): Customer Impact: two customers on dedicated capacity seeing 500s for generation calls, support tickets coming in. cc @leah for comms
leah (eng-oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) remove traffic from affected nodes (cordon+drain), 2) scale down continuous-batcher worker count to cap growth, 3) enable emergency config to cap batch_size and kv_cache retention
sam (eng-runtime): attempting hotfix to batcher config: setting CONT_BATCH_MAX_ACCUM=200000 and KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=6GiB. Pushing to canary group now:
```kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/continuous-batcher CONT_BATCH_MAX_ACCUM=200000 KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=6GiB --record```
incident-bot: deployment rollout started by sam (eng-runtime) — rollout id r-20260315-001
leah (eng-oncall): cordoning ip-10-0-12-45 and draining pods to new nodes to avoid noisy neighbor. ```kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-45 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```
raj (eng-sre): pods on that node were hitting `SIGKILL` repeatedly, kernel logs show page allocation failures before container OOMs. suspect prefetch+kv growth causing paging to host and GPU memory pressure -> cuda oom
sam (eng-runtime): canary config applied, I see accumulator cap enforcement in canary logs: ```INFO batcher: truncating accumulator to 195k tokens; evicted 20 entries from kv-cache```
carlos (prod-support): support update draft: "We're investigating elevated 5xx errors for generation in us-west; mitigation in progress, updates in 30m." Want me to post now?
leah (eng-oncall): yes post now, include that dedicated customers may see degraded performance, we're doing rolling mitigations. tag SRE/Runtime for root cause analysis
ops-bot: Pager duty note — oncall shift handoff in 25m, leah, do you want to hand to night oncall?
leah (eng-oncall): I'll stay for the handoff, but if we still have noisy nodes at 09:30 we'll escalate to second tier. Raj please keep the node cordon until we validate kernel memory throttling isn't happening
raj (eng-sre): will do. also opening a host-level ticket to disable transparent hugepages on those nodes as a short-term experiment — attaching steps to the incident thread
sam (eng-runtime): patch candidate to enforce kv-cache caps merged to hotfix branch: ```git cherry-pick -x abc123 && ./deploy/hotfix.sh r-20260315-001``` — rolling across remaining nodes now
incident-bot: Hotfix rollout 60% complete — 3/5 node pools updated
leah (eng-oncall): metrics trending down: 95p latency dropped from 11.2s -> 2.1s after canary. error rate down to baseline on canary. continue rollout but keep drains until stable
carlos (prod-support): posted customer update, ticket queue is calmer. tagging customers impacted to notify them of mitigation and next update in 2h
leah (eng-oncall): follow-up items: - postmortem required (assign to sam/raj) - reproduce locally with long tail prefix sequences to validate accumulator eviction bug - add automated alarm for kv_cache_bytes growth beyond 8GiB - revisit default kv_cache caps for Dedicated tiers
sam (eng-runtime): noted. creating issue: "cb-kvcache-runaway-accumulator" and linking incident id INC-20260315-001
raj (eng-sre): nodes remain cordoned until we've validated no paged memory flapping. I'll uncordon one node tomorrow during low traffic window after kernel tweak
leah (eng-oncall): thanks all. leaving thread open for postmortem links and RCA. I'll handover to night oncall at shift change if nothing else pops up
ops-bot: SHIFT HANDOFF: leah -> morgan (eng-oncall). morgan oncall at 09:30 PDT.
leah (eng-oncall): handing to morgan, summary: continuous-batcher kvcache runaway -> cuda OOM -> node flares; mitigated via accumulator caps, kv_cache cap, cordon/drain, hotfix rollout. watch list: kv_cache_bytes, batch accumulator length, pod OOMs
incident-bot: Incident closed to active response; postmortem required within 72h.
leah (eng-oncall): closing thread — will attach postmortem link once sam/raj create it. :white_check_mark:
